items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: when you play, we both playing together... such as, uh, Peter Bugga

ctx.x: It had to be his dry lips. Like when you play, we both playing together, well, he'd say hold it for a while. You see, all you say hold it. Well, you hold it, you sit on it, take a rest day, you move on. By the time I come back in, that's the way I'll figure it out. But for instance, a solo now, I don't know, it's different. Uh-huh. Yeah, pretty much all of them in the ground is different. It's hard to get a, uh, a real Dixieland man who's out there for us to find out, you catch some of the first men, such as, uh,…
Uh-huh. Yeah. Well, now, I mean, back in the old days when you would play, take the lead, would the people applaud after you finished taking the clarinet part alone like you do now?
